tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now. "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Continue you automatically to report once this session (and any sibling still working) finishes and you are idle. Only when the user asked to be told; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud".

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. It starts from this session's pushed branch when it runs in a worktree, else the repository's default branch. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). Must exist; if the user has not trusted it yet the app asks them first. "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one. Self-hosted environments and runner pools need the user's own click and are refused, and so is an environment that cannot run this project's repository.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from (default: the checkout's current branch). Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. # Calm Registry

A mobile-first baby registry that builds itself from a short chat. Parents answer a few
tap-to-answer questions, get a full registry with products from Amazon, Walmart, and Target,
review it one category at a time, edit it in plain language, and share a link with family.

## Run locally

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Every key is optional locally. Without them the app uses a scripted chat, sample products,
and stores data in `.data/registries.json`. See `.env.example` for all settings.

## Production (Vercel)

Supabase is required in deployed environments because Vercel's filesystem is read-only.

1. Apply `supabase/migrations/*.sql` to your Supabase project.
2. Set `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, and
   `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` in Vercel.
3. Add the Vercel domains to Supabase Auth's redirect URLs so magic links work.
4. Optionally add `OPENAI_API_KEY` and retailer keys to replace the scripted chat and
   sample products.
5. Optionally add `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` to turn on voice mode ("Talk instead" in the intake
   chat and the mic in the edit box). The key needs at least Member permission so the
   server can mint 30-second tokens. The browser connects straight to Deepgram's Voice
   Agent API with that token; the agent's AI runs on Deepgram's hosted `gpt-4o-mini`.

content.text:
# UX audit: Calm Registry

I went through the home page, the intake chat, the registry overview, the review flow and the family share page. I checked them at phone width (375) and on your laptop (1290), using your local data, and read the code for each screen. I didn't change any code or data.

## Fix first: these break trust

**1. Family can see items you haven't reviewed yet.** The share link shows everything except skipped items, so all 25 unreviewed draft items appear on `/r/…`. Someone could buy a gift you were about to skip. The filter at [route.ts:15](app/api/r/[slug]/route.ts:15) should keep only kept items. The overview has the same problem: "25 items, about $1,851" counts items you haven't reviewed as if they're on the list.

**2. Quantities count as one gift.** Glass bottles ×4 or swaddles ×3 get marked "Gifted" as soon as one person buys one. The button says "$44.99 at Target" with nothing about the ×4, so it's unclear whether that's the price for one or for all four. Family needs to see "1 of 4 bought" and be able to mark a partial purchase.

**3. Several taps are instant and can't be undone:**
- "Remove" on the overview deletes the row straight away.
- Keep and Skip in review have no way back to the previous item.
- Tapping an alternative product replaces the chosen one with no selected state, so it looks like the list just reshuffled.

Showing an "Undo" toast after Remove and after each Skip would cover most of this.

## Fix next: friction

**4. Returning users lose the home page.** With 9 registries, the "Your registries" box fills the whole first screen on a phone, and the headline and "Start my registry" are pushed below the fold. Titles get cut off on mobile and repeat ("Our Baby Registry" twice, three "Welcome Baby…"), with no date, item count or progress to tell them apart. Fixes:
- Show 2–3 registries with "See all".
- Add one line under each: "25 items · 0 reviewed · made Oct 7".
- When you have registries, put the primary action on the newest one rather than on "Start".

**5. Part of the laptop sidebar is out of reach.** On the overview at 1290×800, the sticky sidebar is 899px tall, so the "Change your registry" input sits below the screen until you scroll to the very bottom of the item list. A proposed change makes the sidebar taller still. Either let the sidebar scroll on its own, or move "Change your registry" to the top of the right-hand column.

**6. The review start screen doesn't say where to begin.** It lists 10 categories that all say "about 1 min", with no button to start. Add "Start with Sleep" as the main button and keep the list for jumping around. On phones the category rows have no arrow or other sign that you can tap them.

**7. The overview mixes two jobs.** Editing (names, answers, review, share, change box) is stacked above the list on mobile, so the items start around 650px down. The sticky change bar also covers part of each row. When there are still items to review, "Continue review" should be the one clear action, and sharing should wait until the review is done. Sharing a draft is how issue 1 reaches family.

## Polish

- **Edit box placeholder is cut off on mobile.** "We're getting a hand-me-down stroller" shows as "re getting a hand-m". Use something shorter, like "What's changed?".
- **Product names don't fit the placeholder tiles.** When there's no photo, the tile shows the item name, and long ones like "Natural Baby Shampoo and Body Wash" spill past the 72px tile. Alternatives with no photo show an empty dashed box. Both should show a tinted tile with a single letter or category mark.
- **Alternatives are hard to tell apart.** At 375 they cut off to "Puddle Duck Organic …", which looks the same as the chosen product. Show brand and price, and wrap the name.
- **The "why" note is hidden on phones** in the overview rows, even though it's what makes this product different. A one-line clamp would keep it.
- **The intake chat's "…" is a bare ellipsis.** It doesn't tell you anything is loading. Animated dots, or "Thinking about your answers", would read better.
- **Gift links switch straight into a confirm step.** "$27.99 at Target" opens the store in a new tab and also turns the card into "Did you buy it?" right away. When people come back without buying, that prompt looks like they already did something. Show it only when they return to the tab, and word it "Did you buy it at Target?"

## What's working
- Calm, specific copy: "Nothing is built until you say so", and errors that tell you what to do next.
- Tap-to-change answers in the chat.
- Writing a change in plain language and approving it before anything happens.
- No horizontal overflow at the sizes I checked.

If you want me to fix these, I'd do 1–3 first because they affect real gifts, then 4–6.

content.text:
I agree, though the problem isn't tight spacing. The margins are generous. It's that too many things on each screen look equally important, so nothing leads. The review card and the intake chat feel calm because each shows one thing at a time. The overview, the share page and the home page for returning users don't.

**The registry overview is the most crowded.** The sidebar stacks seven blocks, each a label and a button of the same weight: Edit details, Change answers, Continue review, Share link, the suggestion chips, the voice invite and the change box. On a phone all of that sits above the items. A fixed bar at the bottom (chips, text field, mic, Change) then covers part of each row, so you're always reading around controls.

**Each item row has six lines.** Name and price, product title and store, stars with "Read reviews", the italic reason, and "Remove". With an underlined link or two on every row, a list of 25 items becomes a column of underlines. The rose italic reason is lovely on its own, but it shows up everywhere and stops standing out.

**The share page repeats the same pattern.** Each card has stars, a reviews link, the reason, a price button and "I bought it somewhere else". Relatives just need to see what it is, why it's on the list, and where to buy it.

**Home with saved registries** shows a "Delete" and an "Open" on every row, so nine registries means 18 buttons before the headline.

What I'd do is cut things rather than add space:
- **Overview:**
  - Show one main action based on where you are: "Continue review" until you're done, then "Share link".
  - Fold the details and answers into a single "Registry settings" line.
  - Turn the bottom bar into a single "Change something" button that opens the voice room or a text field.
- **Item rows:** keep name, price and the reason. Move ratings to the review card, where you're actually deciding, and put Remove in a small menu on each row.
- **Share page:** make the stars themselves the link to reviews, and drop the separate "Read reviews" link.
- **Home:** show the two newest registries with "See all", and move Delete into each registry's settings.

Want me to start with the overview? It would make the most difference.

content.text:
I've cleared up the registry overview, and star ratings now only show on the keep-or-skip card. I committed and pushed it as `11baa46`.

**Star ratings** are gone from the overview and from the page family sees. They now only appear on the keep-or-skip card, along with the other product choices.

**Overview, top to bottom:**
- **Title and one summary line.**
- **One next step.** While items are still unreviewed, it's a "25 items still to review" card with "Continue review". Once everything is reviewed, it becomes "Share with family and friends" with a "Share link" button.
- **A "Registry settings" row** that opens to show names, shipping address, your answers, start over and delete. While you're still reviewing, the share link is in there too. If someone asks for your address, that request still shows outside the settings, since it needs an answer.
- **"Change your registry" is a single button** plus the mic button. Tapping it opens the suggestions and the text box, which close again once a change is applied.
- **Item rows have three lines:** name and price, the reason (now visible on phones too), and the product and store with a quiet "Remove". There are no more underlines in the list.

**How it checks out:**
- On a phone, the first item now starts about halfway down the screen. Before, it started more than a full screen down.
- On your laptop the sidebar is 552px tall instead of 899, so the change button is no longer cut off below the screen.
- At 320, 375, 768, 1024, 1290 and 1920 wide, neither the overview nor the share page scrolls sideways, and neither shows any ratings.
- Placeholder tiles for items without photos now hyphenate long names instead of spilling out of the tile.

To check the fully reviewed state, I temporarily marked one local registry as reviewed, then restored your data file from a backup.

1. **Categories start collapsed.** Each header shows the category name, how many items it has, its subtotal, and a row of small product photos, so the whole registry fits on about one screen. Tapping a category opens it, there's an "Open all / Close all" control, and the page remembers which ones you had open.
2. **Two columns of items on laptops,** so an open category takes half the scrolling.
3. **"Still needed / Gifted" filter,** which shows up once gifts start coming in. That's when parents actually come back to this page.
4. **Undo after Remove.** Right now it removes the item instantly with no way back.

content.text:
The item list on the overview is now much shorter: on your laptop the whole registry fits on one screen. I committed and pushed it as `9a837d1`.

**What changed:**
- **Categories start collapsed.** Each one is a single row with its name, how many items it has, its subtotal, how many have been gifted, and up to five product photos. Tap a row to open it. "Open all / Close all" sits at the top, and the page remembers which categories you left open on that device.
- **Open categories use two columns on wide screens** (about 1280px and up), so an open category needs half the scrolling.
- **Once a gift has been marked bought,** a "Still needed / Gifted" filter appears at the top, next to "All". Picking one opens every category and shows only the matching items. Before any gifts, it just says "Your list".
- **Remove now shows "Removed Diaper Cream · Undo"** for about 6 seconds.
- **Collapsed rows only show real product photos.** Items without a photo don't leave empty tiles.
- **A category with no prices shows no subtotal,** instead of "$0".

I tested opening a category, filtering to gifted items, and removing and then restoring an item. None of the widths from 320 to 1920 scrolls sideways, even with every category open. Your data is back to how it was. I'd temporarily marked some items reviewed and gifted to test the filter.

**Ideas I didn't build** (say if you want any):
- **Add-to-cart links grouped by store.** "Buy the 8 things still needed at Target" would take one tap instead of eight.
- **"Most wanted" labels.** Parents could pin a few items, and they'd show first on the family page.
- **Sort within a category** by price or by what's most needed.
- **Each gift's giver and date in the Gifted view,** which you could use as a thank-you-note list.

content.text:
Item rows now lead with the actual product, the quantity is editable, and the list no longer stretches across your laptop screen. On the deployed site, though, the quantity buttons won't save until the new database migration is run in Supabase. I committed and pushed it as `9931451`.

**The row now looks like this:**
```
[photo]  WaterWipes Sensitive+ Newborn & Baby Wipes
         $15.97 each at Amazon
         [ − 8 + ]   Remove
```
- **The product name is the headline,** and both the photo and the name open the product page.
- **The store sits with the price,** right under the name: "$15.97 each at Amazon". "Each" only appears when the quantity is more than one.
- **The generic "Wipes" label and the reason sentence are gone.** The category heading already says what group it's in, and the reason still shows on the keep-or-skip card.
- **The quantity is a − / + stepper** that saves straight away and goes from 1 to 20.
- **Items with no exact product match** show their own name and "Find it at Amazon" instead.
- **Gifted items** show a "Gifted" tag instead of the stepper.

**Width:** your screenshot is the widest layout, where each row was about 680px with the price stranded on the far right. Open categories now use:

| Screen | Columns |
|---|---|
| Phone | 1 |
| Tablet | 2 |
| Small laptop | 1 (next to the sidebar) |
| Laptop around 1290 | 2 |
| Wide laptop (like yours) | 3 |

Rows are now about 300–380px wide on laptops. Nothing scrolls sideways at any width from 320 to 1920. I checked that the quantity saves (4 to 5), then put your local data back.

**Run this migration before the next deploy:** [20261010120000_item_quantity.sql](supabase/migrations/20261010120000_item_quantity.sql). Your Melody registry isn't in the local data, so it's probably on Supabase. Until that file is applied there, the stepper will show an error instead of saving.

content.text:
Here's a brief you can paste to the other agent:

---

**Task:** Apply one SQL migration to the production Supabase database for the Calm Registry app.

**Why:** The registry overview page now has a − / + quantity stepper on each item. When it's clicked, the app calls a Postgres function, `public.registry_set_item_qty`. That function doesn't exist in production yet, so the stepper currently shows an error instead of saving.

**Where:**
- Repo: `/Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/baby-registry`, branch `main`, commit `9931451`
- Supabase project ref: `jornrewihrxtotkjtaad`
- SQL editor: https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/jornrewihrxtotkjtaad/sql/new

**What to run:** the full contents of `supabase/migrations/20261010120000_item_quantity.sql`. It does three things:
1. Creates `public.registry_set_item_qty(p_registry_id uuid, p_owner_id uuid, p_item_id uuid, p_qty integer)`. It checks that the owner owns the registry, updates `registry_items.qty`, and increments the registry's revision number. That revision bump is what triggers the live-update broadcast to the family share page.
2. Revokes execute on it from `public`, `anon` and `authenticated`.
3. Grants execute to `service_role` only, matching the other `registry_*` functions.

**Safety:**
- It only adds a function. No tables, columns or existing rows change.
- It uses `create or replace`, so running it twice is safe.
- It depends on `private.lock_owned_registry` and `private.bump_revision`, which earlier migrations already created. The `qty between 1 and 20` check on `registry_items.qty` already exists too.
- This is the production database, so get the user's OK before running.

**How to apply:** pick one.
- **SQL editor:** paste the file into the editor linked above and click Run.
- **Supabase CLI:** `supabase link --project-ref jornrewihrxtotkjtaad`, then `supabase db push`. This needs the CLI installed and logged in, plus the database password.
- **psql:** run the file against the project's database connection string. That string isn't in Vercel's environment variables (only `SUPABASE_URL` and the API keys are), so get it from Supabase's dashboard under Settings → Database.

**How to verify:**
- In the SQL editor, run `select proname from pg_proc where proname = 'registry_set_item_qty';`. It should return one row.
- Or open a registry overview on the live site, open a category, and click + on an item. Reload the page and the new quantity should still be there.

---

content.text:
I agree on the reason sentence, and I'll remove it from this card too. Here's what I'd also change for dim screens:

- **The photo is the biggest issue.** Product photos sit on a lavender background, and a blending effect makes their white backgrounds take on that tint. That also tints the product: the driftwood crib reads slightly purple, and light products lose their edges at low brightness. That's a problem on the one screen where you're judging the actual color, like driftwood versus white. I'll show product photos on white with a thin border here, so the colors are accurate.
- **Gray text is a little faint.** "Needed in the first weeks", "Amazon" and the alternative prices are light gray at 13px, which fades on a dim screen. I'll darken the gray across the app and make the small text a bit bigger.
- **Borders and the progress track are almost invisible.** Divider lines are only 12% opacity, so the progress bar track and card outlines disappear. I'll make them a little stronger.
- **The alternatives' photos are tiny** (44px). I'll make them bigger so you can actually compare.

content.text:
I removed the reason sentence from the keep-or-skip card and made the card easier to read on a dim screen. Committed and pushed as `5e044aa`.

- **Photos show their true colors.** The main photo and the alternatives' photos now sit on white with a thin border. Before, the lavender background blended into the product, so the driftwood crib looked slightly purple and light products lost their edges on a dim screen. The small thumbnails elsewhere keep the pastel tints, since there you're just recognising the item, not judging its color.
- **Gray text is darker everywhere,** and small text on this card is a size bigger: "Needed in the first weeks", the store name, the alternative prices and "Or choose a different one".
- **Borders, card outlines and the progress bar track are more visible.** Before, they nearly disappeared at low brightness.
- **Alternatives are easier to compare.** Photos are bigger (56px, up from 44), and names wrap to two lines instead of being cut off.

I checked the card on a laptop and a phone, and neither scrolls sideways. The darker gray and borders are a global change, so they'll show on every page.

Someone else is editing `lib/types.ts`, `lib/profile.ts`, `lib/answers.ts` and `lib/registry-store.ts` right now, and their changes currently cause type errors. I left all four out of my commit.

content.text:
The app now has a "My registries" sidebar, and product photos no longer have colored backgrounds. Committed and pushed as `88ec70b`.

**Navigation**
- **On a laptop**, a sidebar on the left has:
  - Calm Registry
  - a **New registry** button
  - a **My registries** list, with the registry you're viewing highlighted
- **Unfinished answers** show in the list as "A new registry, 3 answers so far", with an × to discard them.
- **The collapse button** shrinks the sidebar to a slim strip with each registry's first letter (hover to see the full name). It stays collapsed until you open it again.
- **On a phone**, a top bar has a **My registries** button that opens the same list as a drawer.
- **Hidden** on the family share page and when you're signed out.
- **The "Your registries" box is gone from the home page.** "Start one using answers from…" now lives in each registry's settings as "Start a new registry using these answers".

**Product photos** now sit on white with a thin border everywhere: the overview, the review card, the home page examples and the family page. I also noted this in my memory of your design preferences, so the tinted backgrounds don't come back.

**Checks**
- I tried the sidebar, the collapse button and the phone drawer.
- At 1024 the sidebar made the home page scroll sideways, and I fixed it. Nothing scrolls sideways now on home, overview, review, the question chat or the family page at any width from 320 to 1920.

**Still open:**
- **Duplicate names.** Several local registries share names like "Our Baby Registry", so the list has look-alike entries. Showing a date or item count under each would need a small API change. I can add it if you want.
- **"Calm Registry" appears twice on the question chat page on a laptop**, once in the sidebar and once in that page's own left column. Another session is editing that file right now, so I didn't touch it.

content.text:
Changing this makes sense, because the panel's message no longer matches the product. "Every item comes with a reason" was the selling point, but we've just taken reasons off the overview, the review card and the family page. The copy beside it has the same problem: "with a note on why each one is there". Here are four directions.

**A. Show the finished list.** Replace the panel with a small preview of a real registry overview: category rows with photo thumbnails, item counts and subtotals ("Sleep, 8 items, $1,019"), and one category open with three product rows. It backs up "finish tonight" by showing what you end up with. It's the safest option, but also the least memorable.

**B. Keep or skip, live.** The panel is a working review card with one real product, its price and store, and Skip and Keep buttons. Tapping either moves on to the next of four or five examples, and a little counter at the end says "4 kept". Visitors try the core step before signing up. It's playful without being toy-like, since it uses the real component.

**C. Your answers change the list.** One question from the chat with tappable answers: "Do you have a car, or will you mostly be walking?" with "We drive" and "Mostly walking" as answer buttons. Tapping one swaps the two or three products underneath. Car seat and travel system for drivers, a carrier and compact stroller for walkers. It shows the thing other registries don't do, which is that the list is built around your life rather than a generic checklist.

**D. Real products, three stores.** A neat grid of six real product photos on white, each with its price and store, mixing Amazon, Target and Walmart. It's simple and credible, and says "real products, buy anywhere". It's closest to what's there now, minus the reasons.

**My pick is C.** It's the most specific to this product, it replaces the "reason" idea by showing the reasoning instead of writing it out, and it gives the page one interactive moment that rewards a tap. B would be my second choice.

**Copy, whichever you pick:**
- **Headline:** keep "A baby registry you can finish tonight". It's a clear, specific promise.
- **Body:** shorten it to "Answer a few questions out loud or by typing. Get a full list of real products from Amazon, Target, and Walmart, then keep or skip each one."
- **Button:** "Start my registry" is good. Add one quiet line under it: "Free. Family never needs an account."

Which direction should I build?
